newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended weak on Friday after taking a fright from Wall Street which fell more than 100 points shortly after the opening, dealers said.
Wall Street's slide jolted the industrial index to end off 30.8 points at 9,283.4, while the all-shares shed 15.2 points to close at 7,599.2.
Dealers said the fall also spurred more profit-taking which had gripped the industrials during most of the day, epitomised by a surge in local and foreign buying interest.
"It's a tough close. The Dow came down a 100 points at the start and profit-taking continued. The market has just been overwhelmed," one dealer at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said.
Dealers said foreign interest was evident in diamond firm De Beers as it ended with volumes up following an asset swap to an offshore buyer.
The stock, however, finished down 625 cents at 171.75, rand as dealers said an unrealistic price set at Thrusday's close was being corrected.
Turnover was 1.3 billion rand compared to 1.9 billion rand on Thursday as 36 shares surged to new highs and 10 fell to new lows.
In the broader market, decliners led advancers by 189 to 185.
A slightly better bullion price, holding firm as bullion pushed its head above $320 and ounce helped resuscitate golds which have grimaced amid current bullion woes at lower levels.
"The gold price is egding up and I think this is good for the gold market," another dealer said.
The gold index added 29.3 points to 996.4.
Dealers said the market's underlying sentiment remained positive on hopes of an imminent interest rate cut with next week's trading seen continuing firm, provided the rand did not weaken further.
Fuels firm Sasol ended unchanged at 59 rand with volumes higher up at 96 million rand after three offshore sale deals by broking firms Fleming Martin, ING Barings and SBC Warburg.

Newly-listed confectionery to snacks firm Afribrand shed 39 cents to close at 278 cents as listing interest started to wane, while electronics firm Persetel added 130 cents to 36.25 rand on 12 billion rand move to merge with electronics firm Q-Data which closed off 90 cents at 10.00 rand.
On the gold board, gold mining firms Eastvaal added 20 cents to close at 490 cents, and Kloof surged 160 cents to end at 25.10 rand.
Dealers said the South Afrian near-dated industrial share futures also took a shock from Wall Street's shaky start, with the gold contracts, however, steaming ahead on a better bullion price.
The September industrial contract was last at 8,695/708 from 8,779 settlement, the gold index last at 695/709 from 685 settlement and the all-shares last at 6,780/90 from 6,806.
